metadata.title: Flashpoint Retail Behavioral Shopping Interviews & Claude Scoring

qa_turns.question: How are you feeling about the national economy, inflation, and your household outlook right now?
qa_turns.answer: Honestly, the country feels like it's in terrible shape. Inflation is out of control, gas and utility bills are frustrating, and with all the government spending and high interest rates, I'm pretty gloomy about where the broader economy is heading in the next 12 to 24 months.

qa_turns.question: What was your last register receipt total here at Costco, and how has your overall spending changed?
qa_turns.answer: My receipt today was $393.32. We bought USDA Prime ribeye steaks, organic olive oil, two cases of Kirkland Prosecco, fresh berries, and a Dyson vacuum on promotion. Honestly, our actual monthly spending hasn't slowed down at all—if anything, we're spending 15% more this year because we love the quality and value.

qa_turns.question: Are you cutting back on discretionary spending or trading down to cheaper store alternatives?
qa_turns.answer: Not really cutting back. We buy Kirkland Signature because the quality is just as good or better than name brands, like the Kirkland French vodka and Italian Parmigiano. We just booked our ski trip to Aspen through Costco Travel. We're definitely not pinching pennies on lifestyle.

qa_turns.question: Do you plan to renew your Costco Executive membership next year, and how often do you shop here?
qa_turns.answer: Oh, 100% renewal without question. The 2% cash back check basically pays for the membership twice over. We come here about 3.8 times a month, usually on Saturday mornings. It's an indispensable routine for our family.
